metaDescription: We compared six ultrasonic cleaner baths from 200 ml to 30 L on frequency, power, heating and timers, so you can match a tank to bench or home use.
introParagraphs: In a lab or workshop the tank of an ultrasonic cleaner is called a bath, and the word has stuck as a search term for any bench machine that fills with water or solvent and shakes dirt loose with sound. The category is wide: a 1.3 L tub meant for rings and a 30 L stainless unit for carburetors are both sold under the same name, which makes a casual search misleading.

We evaluated six baths based on product specs and buyer feedback, looking at frequency, transducer power, heater output, timer range and how each one is filled, emptied and stored. The lineup runs from a 200 ml dental pod to a 30 L parts bath, with 40 kHz VEVOR benchtop units forming the core of the middle range.
Use the picks below as a starting point, then work through the buying criteria and decision tables to match a bath size and heating setup to your items and your bench space.

products.name: VEVOR 3L Heated Ultrasonic Cleaner, 120W 40kHz
products.description:
The VEVOR 3L is the best all-round bath in this group because it covers the middle ground well. Two 60W transducers deliver 120W at 40 kHz into a 3 L (0.8 gal) 304 stainless steel tank, and a digital panel sets a timer from 0 to 30 minutes and heat from room temperature to 80°C (176°F). The listing cites CE, FCC and RoHS certification, and the package includes a cleaning basket.

Practical details help it feel finished: anti-slip rubber feet, dual fuse protection and heat dissipation are all listed. The tradeoff is frequency, since 40 kHz is at the more aggressive end, so it needs care with fragile stones, soft plastics and glued parts. Heat is a plus for oily items but it is something you should leave off for anything delicate.

In use it is a typical fill, set and wait bench machine with a footprint that fits a countertop or a workshop shelf. Compared with the VEVOR 1.3L at 60W it doubles the power and adds heating, and against the VEVOR 6L at 180W it is easier to store and uses far less water. It suits mixed households that clean glasses, watches, tools and small parts.
products.bestFor: Mixed home and hobby use: glasses, watches, jewelry, tools and small parts.
pros: Dual 60W transducers give 120W at 40 kHz in a manageable 3 L tank
Heats from room temperature up to 80°C and times cycles to 30 minutes
Anti-slip feet, dual fuses and heat dissipation add a safety margin
A cleaning basket is included, which protects both items and tank floor
cons: 40 kHz needs care with fragile stones, soft plastics and glued parts
The heater is not suitable for delicate or heat-sensitive items
Not large enough for long tools, big trays or whole carburetors

products.name: VEVOR 1.3L Digital Ultrasonic Cleaner, 60W 40kHz
products.description:
The VEVOR 1.3L is the smallest benchtop bath here and the simplest. It uses a single 60W sandwich-style transducer at 40 kHz and a digital timer from 0 to 30 minutes. The 304 stainless steel tank measures 6.1 by 5.5 by 2.6 inches, which is enough for rings, watches, coins, eyeglasses and small circuit parts.

The low profile of the tank is the main limit, because it is only 2.6 inches deep, so tall items and long tools do not fit. There is also no heater listed, so greasy parts rely on time and detergent. At 40 kHz it shares the more aggressive frequency of the other VEVOR models, which is fine for sturdy metal items but calls for caution with soft stones.

Storage is easy because it is small, so it can live in a drawer between uses. Compared with the VEVOR 3L at 120W it has half the power and no heating, and against the 200 ml UEOFEN it offers a larger tank for glasses and jewelry, though without the dental modes. It is a sensible low-commitment starter.
products.bestFor: Beginners who want a small, simple bench bath for jewelry, watches and coins.
pros: A compact 1.3 L tank is easy to store and uses very little water
A digital timer from 0 to 30 minutes keeps cycles easy to repeat
304 stainless steel tank holds up to regular small-item cleaning
Plugs into a standard 110V outlet with no setup beyond filling
cons: The tank is only 2.6 inches deep, so tall items and tools do not fit
No heater is listed, so greasy parts rely on time and detergent
At 60W it is slower on heavy buildup than the larger VEVOR baths

products.name: CREWORKS 2L Ultrasonic Bath, 60W with Heater
products.description:
The CREWORKS 2L trades a digital screen for two plain knobs, one for a timed cycle of up to 30 minutes and one for heat from 70 to 175°F. It delivers 60W of ultrasonic power and a 100W heater into a 2 L (half gallon) tank. The basket and tank use 304 stainless steel banding, while the exterior uses 201 stainless steel, and nonslip handles help with moving it.

Knobs make it friendly for anyone who dislikes menus and small buttons. The tradeoff is that you set a position rather than a number, so repeating an exact cycle takes judgment. The listing does not state a frequency, so we could not compare it on that point.

It is straightforward to own: fill, turn the dials and wait. Compared with the VEVOR 1.3L at 60W it has a bigger tank and a heater, and against the VEVOR 3L at 120W it has half the transducer power but costs you no menu learning. It is a decent fit for jewelry, glasses, utensils and toys.
products.bestFor: Anyone who prefers dials to screens for jewelry, glasses and small household items.
pros: Two plain knobs set time and heat with no menus or tiny buttons
A 100W heater and 70 to 175°F range help loosen oils and grime
The 2 L tank is larger than the 1.3 L VEVOR and still compact
Nonslip handles make it easier to move and carry between uses
cons: Knob settings are approximate and harder to repeat than digital ones
The listing does not state a frequency, so gentleness is unclear
At 60W it is slower on heavy grease than the 120W and 180W VEVORs

products.name: VEVOR 6L Ultrasonic Cleaner, 180W 40kHz with Heater
products.description:
The VEVOR 6L is the step up into real parts cleaning, with three 60W transducers delivering 180W at 40 kHz and a 200W heater that reaches 80°C (176°F). The 304 stainless steel tank measures 12.8 by 6.9 by 5.9 inches, and a digital panel sets a 0 to 30 minute timer and the temperature. The listing cites FCC, CE, RoHS and UL certification.

That tank length is the real benefit, because it takes longer tools, circuit boards, tableware and dental instruments that a 3 L bath cannot. The cost is bulk and water: it needs a bench and somewhere to drain 6 L. At 40 kHz it is hard on delicate stones and soft materials, so it is a parts machine first and a jewelry machine second.

Filling and starting are simple, but expect a heavier unit that stays in one place. It holds twice the volume of the VEVOR 3L and delivers 60W more power, and next to the 30 L VEVOR it is far easier to handle, though it holds one fifth of the volume. It suits a garage, hobby bench or small repair shop.
products.bestFor: Hobbyists and small shops cleaning tools, circuit boards, tableware and small parts.
pros: Three 60W transducers give 180W of ultrasonic output at 40 kHz
A 200W heater reaches 80°C to help break down greasy buildup
The 12.8 inch tank length takes longer tools and circuit boards
Listed with FCC, CE, RoHS and UL certification for peace of mind
cons: At 40 kHz it is too aggressive for fragile jewelry and soft stones
Takes bench space and needs 6 L of water filled and drained each time
Overkill for a few rings, a pair of glasses or a single retainer

products.name: VEVOR 30L Ultrasonic Cleaner with Knob Control
products.description:
The VEVOR 30L is the biggest bath here, a 30 L 304 stainless steel tank at 40 kHz aimed at carburetors, spray nozzles, small engine parts and other workshop work. It offers a degassing mode, which the listing says removes air from the liquid and improves efficiency by 30 percent, plus dual power settings for delicate or heavy-duty loads. A knob adjusts time and temperature, with a digital display, and a scratch-proof basket and cleaning ball are included.

The listing does not state a wattage, so we judged it on tank size, modes and controls rather than inventing a figure. The tradeoff is scale: it needs a permanent bench, a lot of water and a way to empty it, and the 30 percent claim is a manufacturer figure we treated cautiously. Neutral detergent and warm water are recommended.

In practice it is a shop machine, not a household appliance. Against the VEVOR 6L at 180W it holds five times the volume and adds degassing, but it is much harder to move and drain. For a home user, the VEVOR 3L at 120W is the more realistic purchase.
products.bestFor: Workshops that batch-clean carburetors, nozzles and engine parts and have bench space.
pros: A 30 L tank takes carburetors, nozzles and several parts at once
Degassing mode and dual power settings add control for different loads
A scratch-proof basket and cleaning ball come with the machine
Knob controls with a digital display make adjusting settings simple
cons: Needs a permanent bench spot and a lot of water to fill and drain
The listing gives no wattage, so power is hard to compare directly
Far too large and strong for jewelry, glasses or occasional use

products.name: UEOFEN 45kHz Dental Cleaning Pod, 200 ml with UV
products.description:
The UEOFEN is a different kind of bath, a 200 ml pod for retainers, dentures, mouth guards, aligners and night guards. It runs 45 kHz ultrasonic waves with built-in 254nm UV lights, and it offers a 5 minute quick clean or a 10 minute enhanced clean that alternates 5 minutes of pulse with 5 minutes of continuous ultrasonic. A digital countdown timer shows progress, and it runs under 45 dB.

Two side slots hold items with handles, such as toothbrush heads, and a tweezer is included for hygienic removal. The tradeoff is size: 200 ml fits one appliance at a time, and it is not intended for tools, jewelry trays or glasses. The UV lights are an extra and are not a substitute for rinsing, brushing or your dentist's advice.

It is easy to place on a bathroom counter or bedside table and needs only a little water. Compared with the VEVOR 1.3L at 60W it is gentler at 45 kHz, runs under 45 dB and is sized for dental use, though the VEVOR gives you a bigger tank for glasses and jewelry. Choose it only if oral appliances are the job.
products.bestFor: Retainer, denture and night guard wearers who want a quiet bathroom-friendly bath.
pros: 45 kHz is gentler than the 40 kHz benchtop baths on soft appliance plastics
A 5 minute and a 10 minute mode cover daily and deeper cleans
Runs under 45 dB, so it is easy to use in a bathroom or bedroom
A digital countdown and included tweezer make handling simple
cons: The 200 ml chamber fits one appliance, not glasses or jewelry trays
UV lights are an extra and do not replace rinsing or brushing
Not suitable for tools, parts or any workshop-style cleaning

buyingCriteria.explanation: The bath limits what physically fits, and both length and depth matter, since items need to sit under the liquid line without touching the walls. A bath under 2 L suits rings and watches, 3 L takes glasses and small tools, 6 L suits circuit boards and longer parts, and 30 L is for engine components. The VEVOR 1.3L is only 2.6 inches deep, while the VEVOR 6L measures 12.8 by 6.9 by 5.9 inches and the VEVOR 30L holds 30 L. Measure your longest item before you buy.

Frequency controls how aggressive the cavitation is. Around 40 kHz produces larger, harsher bubbles that suit tools and metal parts, while 45 kHz and above is gentler on fine pieces and appliance plastics. The VEVOR 1.3L, 3L, 6L and 30L all run at 40 kHz, and the UEOFEN runs at 45 kHz. If your items are delicate, favor a higher frequency, and keep the 40 kHz benchtop units for sturdy metal.

Total wattage should rise with tank volume, otherwise a larger bath cleans weakly. Roughly 60W suits a 1 to 2 L bath, about 120W suits 3 L, and about 180W suits 6 L. The VEVOR 1.3L and CREWORKS 2L list 60W, the VEVOR 3L lists 120W from two transducers and the VEVOR 6L lists 180W from three. Compare watts to liters, not just the headline number.

Warm solution loosens oils faster than cold, but heat can harm glued parts, some plastics and delicate stones. Look for a stated heater wattage and a temperature ceiling. The VEVOR 6L offers a 200W heater up to 80°C, the VEVOR 3L reaches 80°C, and the CREWORKS 2L offers a 100W heater from 70 to 175°F. For anything fragile, run cool and short.

A timer lets you run short cycles, which protect delicate items and stop small units from overheating. A 0 to 30 minute range is common, and digital panels let you repeat exact settings while knobs favor simplicity. The VEVOR 1.3L, 3L and 6L all offer 0 to 30 minutes digitally, the CREWORKS 2L uses two knobs up to 30 minutes, and the UEOFEN uses 5 and 10 minute preset modes. Pick the style you will actually use.

General baths are flexible, but purpose-built ones are optimized for one task. A dental pod like the UEOFEN offers UV lights, a 200 ml chamber and set modes, while the VEVOR 30L offers degassing and dual power for workshop work. Match the machine to your main job. If you need both appliance care and parts cleaning, two small machines usually beat one compromise.

howWeEvaluated.title: Frequency and power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated frequency and wattage across the six baths. The VEVOR 6L leads on listed output at 180W from three transducers, the VEVOR 3L offers 120W from two, and the UEOFEN leads on gentleness at 45 kHz. We treated all figures as manufacturer claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Bath size and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at tank volume, dimensions and what each bath can physically hold. The VEVOR 30L holds 30 L, the VEVOR 6L 6 L, the VEVOR 3L 3 L, the CREWORKS 2L 2 L, the VEVOR 1.3L 1.3 L and the UEOFEN 200 ml. Depth was weighed alongside volume.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heating and run controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked heater output, temperature range and timers. The VEVOR 6L lists a 200W heater to 80°C, the CREWORKS 2L a 100W heater from 70 to 175°F, and the VEVOR 3L heats to 80°C. Where a heater wattage was not stated, as on the VEVOR 30L, we did not assume one.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared control styles, included accessories and safety features. The VEVOR 3L lists dual fuses and anti-slip feet, the VEVOR 30L includes a basket and cleaning ball, and the UEOFEN includes tweezers. Knobs and digital panels were each judged on how simple they are for a new user.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit for purpose
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered whether each bath matches a clear job. The UEOFEN suits oral appliances, the VEVOR 1.3L and CREWORKS 2L suit small personal items, and the VEVOR 6L and 30L suit parts. We did not rank on price figures, only on what each model offers for its class.

cards.label: Heated bath
cards.text: A heater warms the solution so oils and soot dissolve faster, which helps with tools, kitchen utensils and engine parts. The risk is heat damage to glued parts, some plastics and delicate stones. In this lineup the VEVOR 6L (200W, to 80°C), VEVOR 3L (to 80°C) and CREWORKS 2L (100W, 70 to 175°F) heat. Choose one for oily items and keep the temperature low for anything fragile.

cards.label: Unheated bath
cards.text: Without a heater the cycle is cooler and safer for sensitive items, but greasy loads take longer or need detergent. The VEVOR 1.3L lists no heater, and the UEOFEN pod lists UV lights rather than heat. Choose one for rings, retainers and light cleaning where gentleness matters more than speed.

howToChoose.note: Pick heat for grease and parts, and no heat for delicate or glued items.

faq.q: What is the difference between an ultrasonic cleaner and an ultrasonic bath?
faq.a: In practice they are the same device. Lab and workshop users call the stainless tank a bath, while retail listings call the whole machine a cleaner. Both use transducers to create cavitation bubbles in liquid. The labeling matters less than tank size, power and frequency.

faq.q: Which bath is best for most people?
faq.a: The VEVOR 3L at 120W with heating to 80°C is the best all-rounder, since it handles glasses, watches, tools and small parts. If you only clean rings and coins, the VEVOR 1.3L at 60W is enough. If you clean tools and circuit boards, the VEVOR 6L at 180W is the better choice.

faq.q: Is 40 kHz too strong for jewelry?
faq.a: It is fine for sturdy metals but harsh for soft or porous stones such as pearls, opals and emeralds. Higher frequencies around 45 kHz are gentler. The VEVOR baths all run at 40 kHz, so keep fragile pieces out, and ask a jeweler when unsure.

faq.q: Do I need to use a cleaning solution?
faq.a: Water alone handles light dirt, and a mild solution helps with oils and heavier grime. For tools and parts, a neutral detergent in warm water works well, which the VEVOR 30L listing specifically recommends. Always check that the solution suits the item's material.

faq.q: Why should items sit in a basket?
faq.a: Resting items directly on the tank floor can scratch the tank and dampen the cavitation reaching the item. A basket suspends the load in the liquid so the sound reaches all sides. The VEVOR 3L and VEVOR 30L include baskets.

faq.q: How long can I run a bath at a time?
faq.a: Most benchtop units top out at 30 minutes per cycle, and short runs of a few minutes are normal. Long continuous runs overheat small units and add little for light dirt. Rest the machine between heavy cycles and never run it without liquid.

faq.q: Can I clean a watch in an ultrasonic bath?
faq.a: Only if it is clearly water resistant and its maker allows it. Watch crystals, seals and glued parts can be damaged by vibration and heat. Metal bracelets are usually the safer thing to clean, taken off the watch head first.
